title: History Says a $10,000 Investment in the QQQ Will Be Worth $66,000 in 10 Years
author: Neil Patel
description: The Invesco QQQ Trust ETF generated a 563% total return over the past decade, translating to a 20.8% annualized return. If this performance repeats, a $10,000 investment could grow to $66,000 in 10 years. The bull case depends on AI delivering on its promise and generating adequate returns on massive capital expenditures, while the bear case warns of decelerating growth and uncertain AI economic benefits.

title: Satya Nadella's Microsoft Stock Jumped 18% in a Week After Azure's Annual Revenue Topped $100 Billion for the First Time. Is It Still a Buy?
author: Justin Pope
description: Microsoft's stock surged 18% following strong Q4 fiscal 2026 earnings, driven by Azure's milestone achievement of $100 billion in annual revenue and 43% growth. The company reported 18% revenue growth to $90 billion and 31% net income growth, with Microsoft 365 Copilot surpassing 30 million paid seats. Despite trading at a higher forward P/E of 25x (up from 19x pre-earnings), analysts expect 15-16% annual earnings growth over the next three to five years, making the stock still attractive for long-term investors.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q4 earnings with 18% revenue growth and 31% net income growth. Azure achieved $100 billion annual revenue milestone with 43% growth. Microsoft 365 Copilot exceeded 30 million paid seats. Stock valuation remains reasonable at 25x forward P/E with expected 15-16% annual earnings growth. Company successfully repositioning as cost-effective AI provider with in-house chips and models.

title: Sundar Pichai Raised Alphabet's Capex Guidance to $205 Billion the Same Quarter Google Cloud's Backlog Hit $514 Billion. Here's Which Number Actually Matters More.
author: Adam Spatacco
description: Alphabet increased its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $205 billion for AI infrastructure while Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion in multiyear enterprise commitments. The article argues that the backlog is more important as it validates the spending, with roughly 90% of Fortune 100 companies using Gemini Enterprise and customer acquisition doubling year-over-year. Google Cloud revenue accelerated 82% YoY with expanding margins, demonstrating that prior AI infrastructure investments are generating returns.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Alphabet demonstrates strong AI market validation through a $514 billion Google Cloud backlog with 90% Fortune 100 adoption, 82% YoY revenue acceleration, and expanding operating margins. While the $205 billion capex raises concerns about negative free cash flow, the pre-sold capacity and strong cash position ($240+ billion) support the investment thesis as a virtuous cycle of infrastructure spending translating into measurable cloud adoption.
